fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled Lua bytecode reaches a tail call; the Proto pointer p is read from the function value at stack position func before any GC or stack reallocation occurs.

fine_trace.code: for (i = 0; i < narg1; i++) setobjs2s(L, ci->func + i, func + i);
fine_trace.note: The function and its arguments are copied down to ci->func, but L->top is not yet updated, so the GC may not see these as roots.

This macro runs luaC_checkGC(L) which can trigger a full garbage collection. Unlike luaD_precall which uses checkstackGCp(L, fsize, func) to preserve the func pointer, this tail-call path uses checkstackGC which does not preserve any pointer across the GC/stack reallocation.

After checkstackGC, func is reset to ci->func. However, the Proto pointer p was read before the GC and may now be dangling if the closure was collected or the stack was reallocated, leading to use-after-free when p->code is accessed.
The stale Proto pointer p is dereferenced to set the saved program counter, causing a use-after-free read of freed memory when the GC collected the closure during checkstackGC.
